newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end up, volume shrinks.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end up, volume shrinks.

text.p: Shanghai copper ended mostly up on Wednesday, but volume shrank with many investors waiting for clear direction after copper on the London Metal Exchange (LME) showed only marginal gains overnight, traders said.
LME copper moved in a narrow range below $2,300. Three months red metal closed the kerb $3 firmer at $2,282 yuan tonne.
Analysts in London saw LME copper rangebound on Wednesday between support at $2,270 and resistance at $2,305/10.
In Shanghai, the most actively traded December 1997 contract ended at 21,200 yuan ($2,557) per tonne, rising 70 yuan.
It opened at 20,220 yuan, hitting an intraday low of 21,170 yuan and a high of 21,300 yuan per tonne.

August was unchanged at 20,700 yuan, September rose 140 to 20,990, October 100 to 21,100, November 100 to 21,200, the January 1997 contract was flat at 21,000 and February put on 240 to 21,250 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 25,320 tonnes from 40,770 tonnes.
Copper opened higher and moved around opening levels for most of the session.

"Some speculative buying for quick profits was responsible for today's gains but volume was thin, indicating a lack of confidence among most investors about further rises in the next few days," one trader said.
Physical copper in Shanghai was around 20,800-20,900 yuan, unchanged from Tuesday's close due to slack buying interest, traders said.
They said consolidation of the local red metal would extend if LME copper lingered around current levels.
Aluminium ended down on some profit-taking with most investors sidelined believing downward potential would be limited, traders said.
August fell 110 yuan to 14,180, September 100 to 14,400, October 250 to 14,400, November 60 to 14,600 and December 160 to 14,560 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell sharply to 980 tonnes from 7,240 tonnes.
